title: Refreshment Samples and Identification of Nonignorable Attrition under Arbitrary Follow-Up Masks
banked_reason: The broader advertised characterization is not delivered; the sound package is subfield, below the field floor (paper-score ceiling 6.5 < 7.4).
gap_reasons: The broader advertised characterization is not delivered.

The recorded proposal promises an A,K criterion for generic dimension, localized degree, positive chambers, and exceptional loci, but this node expressly leaves all of them unresolved (with the four-wave enumeration also open).

The first uncertified case is M*=(0,0,1,1,0,0); without its generic localized standard-monomial basis and exact real chamber decomposition, kappa, the attainable positive chamber counts, and minimality remain unresolved.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived a sound worst-case global-identification iff theorem, a smooth positive ambiguity patch, a binary-T3 finite-fiber theorem with a regular two-completion witness, and special three-stratum and T4 localized singleton-fiber examples. Its prespecified kill test further reduced interval-follow-up binary-T4 schedules to 512 canonical multiplicity vectors, but exact generic localized elimination failed at the first anchor mask M*=(0,0,1,1,0,0). The promised arbitrary-mask criterion, generic degree, positive chamber stratification, exceptional loci, and inclusion-minimality therefore remain open, leaving the result at subfield rather than the field floor.
tldr: Within the stated positive cohort-specific SAN class, fresh entrants at every nondegenerate wave are necessary and sufficient for worst-case global identification, while followed cohorts can identify particular laws without a terminal refresh. For binary four-wave contiguous masks, a new exact reduction shows that three generic copies of each followed type \(23\), \(24\), or \(34\) exhaust its equality and positivity information, reducing all multiplicities to 512 canonical vectors. The special \(M^*=(0,0,1,1,0,0)\) four-wave law is already verified; what remains open is generic localized elimination, all regular positive chamber counts, and inclusion-minimality across the reduced box.
gap: Existing SAN theory identifies the population law when the needed wave-specific refreshment margins are supplied, and selected three-wave analyses show that following refresh cohorts adds constraints. What remains unresolved is whether arbitrary entry/follow-up masks are generically sufficient, how many positive completions remain on regular zero-dimensional chambers, and where singular or positive-dimensional exceptional fibers occur.
fill: Prove the exact tilt and localized rank-one reduction, establish the global iff boundary, use the exact binary three-wave witness and the candidate three-history resultant as anchors, enumerate binary four-wave masks as an early test, and derive either an interpretable criterion or an exact finite decision procedure with positive certificates.
